articles.author: Hedy
articles.description:
You can get your Raspberry Pi’s IP in a few different ways, depending on whether you can access the Pi directly or not. I’ll cover both.

1. If you can plug in a monitor & keyboard
Log into the Pi (default user is often pi):
A) Quick one-liner (most common)
hostname -I

The first address it prints is usually your Pi’s IPv4 address on the LAN (e.g. 192.168.1.50).
B) More detailed
ip addr show

Look under your active interface:
eth0 for wired
wlan0 for Wi-Fi
Find the line with inet:
Example: inet 192.168.1.50/24 → IP = 192.168.1.50.
C) Check if it’s static on the Pi
On Raspberry Pi OS:
Old style (with dhcpcd):
sudo nano /etc/dhcpcd.conf

Look for a block like:
interface eth0
  static ip_address=192.168.1.50/24
  static routers=192.168.1.1
  static domain_name_servers=192.168.1.1

If present …
articles.title: How can I find the static ip of my Raspberry Pi device?

What is a Gateway?
A gateway can be a standalone device (like a router or firewall) or a software component integrated into a server or cloud platform. Its primary function is to ensure data integrity and compatibility while managing the flow of information between networks.
Why Gateways Are Essential
Real-World Examples
Conclusion
In summary, a gateway is a versatile tool that enables communication, security, and efficiency across networks. Whether bridging the internet, securing transactions, or connecting smart devices, gateways are indispensable in our interconnected world. As technology evolves, gateways will continue to adapt, supporting innovations like 5G, AI-driven networks, and the ever-expanding Internet of Things (IoT). Understanding gateways is not just a technical necessity - it's a key to unlocking the full potential of digital transformation.
This article provides a comprehensive overview of gateways, suitable for both beginners and professionals seeking to deepen their understanding of networking fundamentals. Let me know if you'd like to explore specific aspects further!
